Dr. Long is wonderful! She truly cares about your fur baby and is extremely knowledgeable. My dog recently had her spay surgery and everything went perfectly. The clinic called the next day to check on her, and when I sent pictures, Dr. Long personally called to give her opinion. She really makes time for her patients and their owners, which shows how much she cares. I highly recommend this clinic!
I've been bringing my Siberian Husky to Dr. Long for several years now. She's great! Very thorough, explains everything and is compassionate. Great prices too!
Dr. Theresa is wonderful. I’ve been coming here for 20 years and all my pets. Love her.

I brought both of my babies here over the course of several years for surgery, treatments and exams. Dr. Long isn’t the most welcoming or compassionate vet, neither is her staff. There was one or two receptions/assistants that were okay, though. Rosie being one of them.

My Rotti was scheduled for eyelid surgery, for which I paid in advance. The day we arrived for surgery, the receptionist charged me additionally for sedation for larger dogs. From my understanding that was included in the original invoice, but they “mistakenly” left out that fee until the day of. So I paid that undisclosed fee, also I purchased a nail clipping for my girl while she was sedated, since she had really thick nails.

The surgery went well, however she didn’t receive a full nail clipping, but to like one nail. So I asked the Vet what happened, she explained that my girl bled during, so they discontinued it. And from my recollection, I didn’t receive a refund. My girl was also covered in her poop when I picked her up.

I also brought my Pittie here during Covid lockdown. I wasn’t able to accompany him due to their regulations, so I explained the purpose of the visit to the assistant. She then informed me that I’d receive a call from the vet during his visit. When I got the call, I reiterated to the vet, what I previously explained to the assistant, that he had a big lump on the outside of his left paw. She seemed confused like she didn’t see it, and asked was it his elbow? when the lump was CLEARLY VISIBLE on his PAW, and as if I didn’t give a detail description of that. I asked could she FaceTime me so that I could show her, but she wouldn’t make that compromise, so I guess she finally noticed the huge lump on THE OUTSIDE of his LEFT PAW. Her diagnosis was “it just looks like he hit it on something.” That was groundbreaking information! I paid for an exam for her to tell me the obvious. I’m aware he hit it on something. I wanted to be sure the lump wasn’t a tumor/growth or something that would cause him discomfort.

A later visit I brought my Pittie in to get X-rays and I informed Dr. Long and her assistant that he is reactive and cannot be around other animals in there. Immediately after them taking him out the room for his exam, I hear my boy getting worked up, so I jump up and see the assistant just casually walking him past other dogs while he and the other dogs are getting agitated. She pulled at his leash in an almost playful manner like she had no control over a 80lb dog. I don’t think she expected me to come out the room when I did. I called out to him to calm him down and grabbed his leash to help get him to the lab, which was like 15 feet away. While I walked him to the lab, I told the assistant that I just explained to you that he can’t be around other animals. She was completely nonchalant. The way she was pulling at his leash was how someone does when they walk their dog past other dogs and laugh at how the dog is being aggressive. Her vibe was sneaky and off putting. Definitely would not trust her with my dogs after what I witnessed. Side-note, she kinda resembles Dr. Long, she may be her daughter.

Overall, the general care, peace of mind, and prices are not satisfactory. My Dogs were my family, my best friends & my babies! You want to feel reassured when leaving them in someone else’s hands. I’m not saying Dr. Long is a bad vet, however when you factor in everything else, I wouldn’t recommend!
Great employees but terrible parking

💡 Dr. Long is the nicest and kindest veterinarian my dog has ever had! So helpful. She made sure all my questions were answered and even put in a lot of work to help with my dog’s prescriptions. I’m so glad I’ve found this place. This is my new veterinarian home! Thanks DR. LONG! I’ll definitely be back 🐶

I am heartbroken to be writing this, but I feel a responsibility to share our experience.

I had been coming to this clinic for years and trusted Dr. Long with my dog’s care. Unfortunately, over time I noticed a decline in attentiveness, compassion, and attention to detail. That decline became painfully clear during my dog’s final days.

After my dog hit a pole and developed severe eye swelling, Dr. Long referred us to a specialist due to internal bleeding, which I understood. However, shortly after, I brought him back because I was deeply concerned about additional symptoms—labored breathing and abdominal swelling. I was told he was “fine.”

I pushed for further evaluation, at which point Dr. Long reluctantly said, “Fine, you want an X-ray?”—a response that made me feel like an inconvenience rather than a worried pet parent. The X-ray suggested possible cancer. I was shocked. No compassion, explanation, or guidance followed. There was no discussion of palliative care, comfort measures, additional testing, or what to watch for. Not even a follow up.

Only after I begged was my dog sent home with carprofen.

Trusting my instincts, I took him to another veterinarian. They performed abdominal X-rays and immediately told me he was in the final stages of cancer, internally bleeding, and in active distress. They were visibly upset that palliative care had not been discussed and that his comfort had not been prioritized.

My dog crossed the rainbow bridge the following day.

This experience left me devastated—not just by the diagnosis, but by the lack of urgency, empathy, and guidance when it mattered most. End-of-life care requires not only medical knowledge, but compassion and clear communication. Sadly, that was missing here.

Dr. Long, if you read this, I genuinely urge you to reflect on whether it may be time to step back, retire, or bring in additional support. Burnout is real—but animals and their families deserve presence, care, and dignity, especially at the end.

They went above and beyond for our family during this heartbreak and we will never forget the kindness they showed us. Will forever be bringing our babies to Roxford 💙

The prices are affordable compared to other vets in the area and I don’t mind putting down a deposit to schedule because I know they’re in high demand. The doctor has helped a lot with one of our dogs that’s special needs and has a lot of urgent care visits. They also take my Care Credit which helps.
Dr. Long is excellent!!

This place showed no compassion for our family dog. We came in on a Saturday to euthanize our 17 year old chihuahua . She was in pain due to her heart failure, when we arrived we were treated like dust that you pay no mind to. None of their staff were helpful nor did they show common sense or interest for that matter. We were crying and sniffling because our beloved dog was yelping in so much pain that even the other customers there saw us but their staff didn’t even bat an eye or offered tissue. Our dog was suffering and practically suffocating due to the fluid in her little lungs. Yet NOTHING from the staff. Our beloved Chiquita suffered and died on my daughters lap and when that happened their STAFF DID NOTHING a caring woman with a cat on the other side made the heartless and nonchalant staff aware of our existence in their vet office. You think that they would prioritize dying dogs in pain but i suppose not. The cherry on top was that there was a damn workout bra laying there and clumps of animal hair all over the floor…. Awful vet they dont prioritize emergencies or suffering dogs.

This place use to shine amongst the other valley clinics, but now it’s run down and dirty. Over a month ago, while searching for a cost effective spaying for my dog, Emily the receptionist there, offered a website to get a discount voucher for the price of the spaying so we made the appointment at Roxford Vet. When it came time to pick up my pet, they said they didn’t work with the organization that provided the voucher and I would have to pay full price. Though most of the staff was trying to be helpful realizing how they had made a mistake because they didn’t consider my address, the tall blond girl was condescending and just wanted to argue about how it was not their fault. Even after I had already settled the payment with the vet herself she was still arguing with me. Needless to say, I definitely will not be coming back and will continue with Dill Veterinary.
